info.name: AppNation case: AI jobs with credits
info.description:
The case's verification flow and API checks. Start the stack first (docker compose up -d --build), then run the whole collection with the Collection Runner: requests that wait for a job ask again every second until it finishes, which only works in the Runner. Every run uses a new user (folder 0).

What Postman cannot see (provider call counts, concurrency, killing the worker, memory) is checked by: docker compose run --rm verify all

item.name: 0. Start
item.description: Run this first. Every run uses a new user, so the collection can run again and again.

exec: // A new user and texts for every run: an input sent before would be answered from the stored result.
pm.test('database and cache are up', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.include({ database: 'up', cache: 'up' }));

item.name: 1. A summary costs 3 credits
item.description: Case: add 10 credits, summary of "merhaba" -> 202, completed shortly afterwards, balance 7.

request.description: Asks again every second until the job finishes (Collection Runner).

exec: // Still queued or processing: ask again in a second (Collection Runner only).

item.name: 2. The same request twice
item.description: Case: same key and body -> same jobId, balance 7; same key, different body -> 422.

exec: pm.test('balance is still 7: nothing charged twice', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().balance).to.eql(7));

item.name: 3. The provider refuses: fail deneme
item.description: Case: fail deneme -> failed; credits are refunded.

exec: // Remembers the balance before the job, to check what it cost.
// Still queued or processing: ask again in a second (Collection Runner only).
pm.test('job is failed (after ' + tries + ' s)', () => pm.expect(job.status).to.eql('failed'));

item.name: 4. The provider fails twice, then answers: flaky deneme
item.description: Case: flaky deneme -> completed after 3 attempts (the attempts show in the worker log: docker compose logs worker | grep <jobId>).

exec: // Remembers the balance before the job, to check what it cost.

request.description: Takes about 5 seconds: two failures with 1 s and 2 s waits.

exec: // Still queued or processing: ask again in a second (Collection Runner only).
pm.test('result is a translation', () => pm.expect(job.result).to.match(/^Çeviri: flaky deneme/));
pm.test('charged once: balance ' + before + ' -> ' + credits.balance, () => pm.expect(credits.balance).to.eql(before - (1)));

item.name: 5. The provider never answers: hang deneme
item.description: Case: hang deneme -> failed after 3 timeouts of 10 s; credits are refunded. Takes about 35 seconds.

exec: // Remembers the balance before the job, to check what it cost.
// Still queued or processing: ask again in a second (Collection Runner only).
pm.test('job is failed (after ' + tries + ' s)', () => pm.expect(job.status).to.eql('failed'));

item.name: 6. Twenty jobs with the same text
item.description: Case: 20 jobs with the same input -> the provider is called once, 20 jobs completed. Postman sees that all 20 complete and 20 credits are spent; that the provider was called ONCE is only in the database and the worker log (docker compose run --rm verify same-text shows it).

exec: // Sends 20 jobs at the same moment, before this request's own (the last one).
pm.sendRequest({ url: base + '/internal/users/' + user + '/credits', method: 'POST', header: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ type: 'translate', input: 'ayni metin ' + run }) } }, () => {});
// Notes the ids of this step's 20 jobs: the newest 20 of the user.
// Looks at the user's newest jobs until the 20 jobs of this step have finished.
pm.test('same text: all 20 jobs completed', () => pm.expect(step.filter((job) => job.status === 'completed').length).to.eql(20));

item.name: 7. Thirty different jobs
item.description: Case: 30 different jobs -> the highest concurrent call count in the logs does not exceed 4. Postman sees all 30 complete; the concurrency is in the worker log: docker compose logs worker | grep maxConcurrent.

exec: // Sends 30 jobs at the same moment, before this request's own (the last one).
pm.sendRequest({ url: base + '/internal/users/' + user + '/credits', method: 'POST', header: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ type: 'translate', input: 'metin ' + i + ' ' + run }) } }, () => {});
// Notes the ids of this step's 30 jobs: the newest 30 of the user.
// Looks at the user's newest jobs until the 30 jobs of this step have finished.
pm.test('different texts: all 30 jobs completed', () => pm.expect(step.filter((job) => job.status === 'completed').length).to.eql(30));

item.name: 8. Kill the worker in the middle of a job (half manual)
item.description:
Case: while slow deneme is processed, docker compose kill worker, then docker compose start worker -> job completed, single capture.

Run "Create summary: slow deneme", then within 5 seconds in a terminal:

    docker compose kill worker && docker compose start worker

Then run "Wait until completed" (it waits up to 90 s). The job must complete and the balance drop by exactly 3.

request.description: Now kill and start the worker: docker compose kill worker && docker compose start worker

exec: // Remembers the balance before the job, to check what it cost.
// Still queued or processing: ask again in a second (Collection Runner only).
pm.test('one capture: balance ' + before + ' -> ' + credits.balance, () => pm.expect(credits.balance).to.eql(before - (3)));
